meta.title: Number of Mazda dealers in the USA

prompt: How many Mazda dealers are there in the USA?

clarifications.answer: Mazda is a minor, value player with roughly 2% US market share, cars in the $15,000-30,000 bracket.
Take the average US household size as 2.5 people.
Assume an average car lifespan of about 6 years and ~1% annual population growth.
Assume a dealer sells about 50 cars a month, i.e. 600 a year.

common_traps: Estimating the stock of cars but forgetting to convert it into annual sales via replacement plus growth.
Applying Mazda's market share to the whole car market instead of the low-end segment it competes in.
Skipping dealer throughput, so the car count is never turned into a dealer count.

anchors.1: Guesses a dealer count with no households-to-cars-to-dealers chain.
anchors.3: Builds a car-sales estimate but omits either the replacement/growth step or dealer throughput.
anchors.5: Chains households to low-end car stock to annual sales to Mazda's share to dealers via throughput.

anchors.1: Treats all cars and households identically.
anchors.3: Segments cars but with ownership factors not clearly reasoned.
anchors.5: Isolates the low-end segment Mazda competes in and applies its share there.

anchors.1: Botches the stock-to-flow (replacement) conversion; lands far outside a plausible range.
anchors.3: Reaches a number with a slip, landing just outside 400-700 dealers.
anchors.5: Carries the replacement-plus-growth and share math cleanly, landing near 550-570 dealers.

anchors.3: Mentions a check but does not complete it.
anchors.5: Cross-checks that ~570 dealers each selling ~600 cars a year matches the ~3.4 lakh Mazda cars estimated.
